title: Twelve Years and One Rate
subtitle: 货币与支付 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 货币与支付（社会服务与人际沟通·货币与金融）
meta: 主题语境：货币与支付（社会服务与人际沟通·货币与金融）　|　核心词汇：currency　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 currency 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my grandfather ① changed a currency that no bank in the province would have quoted, and he said the changing was the whole of the trade. The ② currency, meaning the money and not the rate, ran twelve years and stayed uncounted; currency, he said, is the only thing in a market that is judged by how long it is left unchanged.

Every ③ currency in that town had the same rate against it, and the ④ currency at the end, meaning the one he kept for the border trade and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever trusted twice. Currency, my grandmother said, is nine parts trust and one part somebody willing to accept; my grandfather said the accepting is the part that fills twelve years.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the currency was the whole of the exchange, meaning the rate and not the money. The ⑥ currency, meaning the rate and not any of that, is the only thing in an exchange that everybody quotes and nobody believes; currency, she said, is either something you change or the only word that means both a money and a rate. He said the rate is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ currency had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the rate. The ⑧ currency of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in August, was one market and twelve years of accepting; currency, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to accept. She said the accepting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ currency I remember is the one at the end, which was withdrawn in 1977 and is still described as the steadiest in the province. A ⑩ currency, my grandmother said in 1979, is the only thing that improves by being trusted; every currency, she said, is a rate that has agreed to look like a money. She said the rate was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 货币；通货（指在市场上流通的那一国货币）
B. n. 货币（指那些钱本身，与那个汇率相对）
C. 固定搭配：change a currency 兑换一种货币
D. n. 货币（指留作边境贸易用的那一种）
E. n. 货币；通货（抽象总称，指一个市场的全部流通手段）
F. n. 货币（指账簿上写到、被记下的那一种）
G. n. 汇率；兑换率（指交易所里报出的那一个）
H. n. 汇率（抽象总称，指被报价的那个比率）

items.q: changed a currency that no bank in the province would have quoted
The currency, meaning the money and not the rate
the currency was the whole of the exchange
the currency had become a line in a ledger
The currency of the whole thing
A currency, my grandmother said in 1979

answers.why: change a currency 意为“兑换一种货币”，1961 年祖父兑换了一种全省没有一家银行会报出牌价的货币。
currency 意为“货币”，指那些钱本身而不是那个汇率，它流通了十二年而从未被清点。
currency 意为“货币”，指那个镇上流通的每一种货币，每一种都有同一个汇率对着它。
currency 意为“货币”，指留作边境贸易用的那一种，是唯一有人信任过两次的。
currency 意为“汇率、兑换率”，指交易所里报出的那一个，母亲说这个汇率就是整个交易所的全部。
currency 意为“汇率”，指被报价的那个比率而不是别的，是交易所里人人都报、却无人相信的东西。
currency 意为“货币”，指账簿上写到、被记下的那一种，到 1969 年这种货币成了账簿里的一行。
currency 意为“货币、通货”，祖父八月写道，整件事的通货是一个市场和十二年的接受。
currency 意为“货币”，我记得的是末尾那一种，1977 年被停用，至今仍被说成全省最稳的。
currency 为抽象总称，祖母 1979 年说，一种货币是唯一会因为被信任而变得更好的东西。
